lines.text: In May 2026, the CEO of Anthropic said something almost no CEO ever gets to say.
lines.say: In May of twenty twenty-six, the CEO of Anthropic said something almost no CEO ever gets to say.

lines.text: “We tried to plan very well for a world of 10x growth per year. And yet we saw 80x.”
lines.say: We tried to plan very well, for a world of ten-x growth per year. And yet... we saw eighty-x.

lines.text: Five months later, the same company revealed this number.
lines.say: Five months later, the same company revealed this number.

lines.text: A loss of $80.7 billion. In six months.
lines.say: A loss of eighty point seven billion dollars. In six months.

lines.text: But before we get to that number, you need to understand just how strong this company really is.
Exhibit one: speed.
lines.say: Exhibit one. Speed.

lines.text: At the start of 2025, Anthropic’s revenue was running at about $1 billion a year.
lines.say: At the start of twenty twenty-five, Anthropic's revenue was running at about one billion dollars a year.

lines.text: By the end of the year: $9 billion.
lines.say: By the end of the year... nine billion.

lines.text: February: $14 billion. April: $30 billion. May: $47 billion.
lines.say: February: fourteen. April: thirty. May: forty-seven.

lines.text: And by the end of July, a run rate of $65 billion a year.
lines.say: And by the end of July... a run rate of sixty-five billion dollars a year.

lines.text: Second-quarter revenue alone topped $11.5 billion — nearly 15 times the same quarter a year earlier.
lines.say: Its second-quarter revenue alone topped eleven and a half billion dollars. Nearly fifteen times the same quarter, a year earlier.

lines.text: Exhibit two: it overtook the leader.
lines.say: Exhibit two. It overtook the leader.

lines.text: For years, OpenAI was the undisputed king of AI revenue. By August, Anthropic’s run rate was reported at $65 billion. OpenAI’s: around $40 billion.
lines.say: For years, OpenAI was the undisputed king of AI revenue. By August, Anthropic's run rate was reported at sixty-five billion. OpenAI's... around forty.

lines.text: In May, investors valued Anthropic at $965 billion — above OpenAI’s last price tag of $852 billion.
lines.say: And in May, investors valued Anthropic at nine hundred and sixty-five billion dollars. Above OpenAI's last price tag, of eight hundred and fifty-two.

lines.text: Exhibit three: business runs on it.
lines.say: Exhibit three. Business runs on it.

lines.text: In a survey by Menlo Ventures — itself an Anthropic investor — Anthropic took 40% of enterprise spending on AI models. OpenAI: 27%. Google: 21%.
lines.say: In a survey by Menlo Ventures, itself an Anthropic investor, Anthropic took forty percent of enterprise spending on AI models. OpenAI, twenty-seven. Google, twenty-one.

lines.text: In coding, its share was 54%.
lines.say: In coding, its share was fifty-four percent.

lines.text: Customers paying more than $1 million a year doubled — from 500 to over 1,000 — in less than two months.
lines.say: Customers paying more than a million dollars a year doubled, from five hundred, to over a thousand, in less than two months.

lines.text: And its coding agent, Claude Code, became a multi-billion-dollar business almost overnight.
lines.say: And its coding agent, Claude Code, became a multi-billion-dollar business, almost overnight.

lines.text: Exhibit four: the giants pay to be in the room.
lines.say: Exhibit four. The giants pay to be in the room.

lines.text: Amazon. Google. Microsoft. Nvidia. All four are investors.
lines.say: Amazon. Google. Microsoft. Nvidia. All four are investors.

lines.text: Amazon put in about $13 billion. By June, it valued that stake at roughly $190 billion.
lines.say: Amazon put in about thirteen billion dollars. By June, it valued that stake at roughly one hundred and ninety billion.

lines.text: And the compute is staggering: up to a million Google TPUs, Amazon’s Project Rainier, a gigawatt on Microsoft Azure.
lines.say: And the compute is staggering. Up to a million Google TPUs. Amazon's Project Rayneer. A gigawatt, on Microsoft Azure.

lines.text: Exhibit five: it’s starting to make money.
lines.say: Exhibit five. It's starting to make money.

lines.text: In both of the first two quarters of 2026, Anthropic reported positive adjusted operating income.
lines.say: In both of the first two quarters of twenty twenty-six, Anthropic reported positive adjusted operating income.

lines.text: Put it all together, and you get one of the fastest climbs in corporate history.
March 2025: $61.5 billion.
lines.say: March, twenty twenty-five. Sixty-one and a half billion.

lines.text: September: $183 billion.
lines.say: September. One eighty-three.

lines.text: February 2026: $380 billion.
lines.say: February. Three eighty.

lines.text: May: $965 billion.
lines.say: May. Nine hundred and sixty-five billion.

lines.text: And now, talk of an IPO at up to $2 trillion.
lines.say: And now... talk of an IPO at up to two trillion dollars.

lines.text: Then came the draft IPO filing — and three numbers that made Wall Street do a double take.
lines.say: Then came the draft IPO filing. And three numbers that made Wall Street do a double take.

lines.text: Revenue, first half of 2026: $16.3 billion.
lines.say: Revenue, for the first half of twenty twenty-six: sixteen point three billion dollars.

lines.text: Net loss: $80.7 billion.
lines.say: Net loss... eighty point seven billion dollars.

lines.text: Cash and short-term investments at the end of 2025: $20.28 billion.
lines.say: And cash and short-term investments, at the end of twenty twenty-five: twenty point two eight billion.

lines.text: Now do the scary math.
$80.7 billion in six months is about $13.5 billion a month.
lines.say: Eighty point seven billion in six months, is about thirteen and a half billion dollars a month.

lines.text: Twenty billion in the bank runs out in about 45 days.
lines.say: Twenty billion in the bank... runs out in about forty-five days.

lines.text: By that logic, the strongest company in AI should have been dead by Valentine’s Day.
lines.say: By that logic, the strongest company in AI should have been dead... by Valentine's Day.

lines.text: So which is it? A rocket… or a bomb?
lines.say: So which is it? A rocket... or a bomb?

lines.text: Let’s take that $80.7 billion apart.
lines.say: Let's take that eighty point seven billion apart.

lines.text: About $72 billion of it is a single accounting line. And not one dollar of it left the company.
lines.say: About seventy-two billion of it, is a single accounting line. And not one dollar of it left the company.

lines.text: It comes from convertible notes: money investors put in that can later turn into shares.
lines.say: It comes from convertible notes. Money investors put in, that can later turn into shares.

lines.text: Imagine a friend lends you $10. Instead of paying it back in cash, you promise shares of your company, at today’s price.
lines.say: Imagine a friend lends you ten dollars. Instead of paying it back in cash, you promise shares of your company, at today's price.

lines.text: Then your company becomes ten times more valuable.
Those shares are now worth $100. On paper, you owe your friend $100.
lines.say: Those shares are now worth a hundred dollars. On paper, you owe your friend a hundred.

lines.text: Accounting rules say that $90 jump is a loss. You didn’t spend a cent.
lines.say: Accounting rules say, that ninety-dollar jump is a loss. You didn't spend a cent.

lines.text: Now scale it up. Anthropic’s valuation went from $380 billion to $965 billion in about three months.
lines.say: Now scale it up. Anthropic's valuation went from three hundred and eighty billion, to nine hundred and sixty-five billion, in about three months.

lines.text: Every leap in value made those notes more expensive — and the reported loss bigger.
lines.say: Every leap in value made those notes more expensive... and the reported loss, bigger.

lines.text: In other words: the stronger Anthropic gets, the more money it appears to lose.
lines.say: In other words. The stronger Anthropic gets, the more money it appears to lose.

lines.text: You can see the other side of this trade on Amazon’s books.
lines.say: You can see the other side of this trade, on Amazon's books.

lines.text: At the end of March, Amazon valued its Anthropic convertible notes at $42.2 billion. By the end of June: $97.9 billion.
lines.say: At the end of March, Amazon valued its Anthropic convertible notes at forty-two point two billion. By the end of June... ninety-seven point nine.

lines.text: A $55.7 billion gain in a single quarter. Same notes. One company books a gain. The other, a loss.
lines.say: A fifty-five point seven billion dollar gain, in a single quarter. Same notes. One company books a gain. The other... a loss.

lines.text: And it isn’t new. Of Anthropic’s roughly $42 billion net loss in 2025, about $34 billion was the same kind of charge.
lines.say: And it isn't new. Of Anthropic's roughly forty-two billion dollar net loss in twenty twenty-five, about thirty-four billion was the same kind of charge.

lines.text: Strip it out, and the $80 billion crater shrinks to under $9 billion.
lines.say: Strip it out, and the eighty billion dollar crater shrinks to under nine.

lines.text: So the loss is fake?
Not so fast.
Because there’s a number in the filing that is very, very real.
lines.say: Because there's a number in the filing that is very... very real.

lines.text: Compute. In the first half of 2025, Anthropic spent $2.3 billion on computing and infrastructure. A year later: nearly $9 billion.
lines.say: Compute. In the first half of twenty twenty-five, Anthropic spent two point three billion dollars on computing and infrastructure. A year later... nearly nine billion.

lines.text: And that’s just the beginning. The filing reportedly lists at least $518 billion of AI-infrastructure commitments over roughly the next decade.
lines.say: And that's just the beginning. The filing reportedly lists at least five hundred and eighteen billion dollars of AI infrastructure commitments, over roughly the next decade.

lines.text: Google: $111 billion.
lines.say: Google. One hundred and eleven billion.

lines.text: Amazon: $110 billion.
lines.say: Amazon. One hundred and ten billion.

lines.text: Microsoft: $31 billion.
lines.say: Microsoft. Thirty-one billion.

lines.text: Nvidia GPUs through smaller cloud providers: about $86 billion.
lines.say: Nvidia chips, through smaller cloud providers. About eighty-six billion.

lines.text: And equipment leases tied to Broadcom: $161 billion.
lines.say: And equipment leases tied to Broadcom. One hundred and sixty-one billion.

lines.text: Roughly 80% of it can’t be cancelled.
lines.say: Roughly eighty percent of it... can't be cancelled.

lines.text: Now put the cash next to it.
$20.28 billion. The bill is about 25 times bigger.
lines.say: Twenty point two eight billion. The bill is about twenty-five times bigger.

lines.text: To be fair, that cash figure is a December snapshot. In 2026, Anthropic announced two more rounds: $30 billion in February, $65 billion in May.
lines.say: To be fair, that cash figure is a December snapshot. In twenty twenty-six, Anthropic announced two more rounds. Thirty billion in February. Sixty-five billion in May.

lines.text: Even so, that’s a fraction of the bill.
lines.say: Even so... that's a fraction of the bill.

lines.text: And look at who sits on both sides of the table.
Amazon and Google invest in Anthropic. Anthropic pays them for cloud. Their stakes rise in value — and Anthropic books a loss.
lines.say: Amazon and Google invest in Anthropic. Anthropic pays them for cloud. Their stakes rise in value... and Anthropic books a loss.

lines.text: The filing even warns that its cloud partners increasingly see Anthropic as a competitor.
And roughly a fifth to a quarter of its revenue came from just two customers.
So: is Anthropic strong, or fragile?
lines.say: So. Is Anthropic strong... or fragile?

lines.text: It depends on which lens you use.
Lens one: the income statement. Here, success looks like failure — the higher the valuation, the bigger the paper loss.
lines.say: Lens one. The income statement. Here, success looks like failure. The higher the valuation, the bigger the paper loss.

lines.text: Lens two: operations. Here, the engine is roaring. Revenue is compounding, and adjusted operating income has turned positive.
lines.say: Lens two. Operations. Here, the engine is roaring. Revenue is compounding, and adjusted operating income has turned positive.

lines.text: Lens three: commitments. Here is the real risk — a half-trillion-dollar bill that comes due whether customers show up or not.
lines.say: Lens three. Commitments. Here is the real risk. A half-trillion-dollar bill, that comes due whether customers show up, or not.

lines.text: The bulls see a company growing faster than almost anything in history, with demand that still outruns supply.
The bears see a fixed bill, concentrated customers, and suppliers who are also rivals. One research firm says the whole company is worth just $144 billion.
lines.say: The bears see a fixed bill, concentrated customers, and suppliers who are also rivals. One research firm says the whole company is worth just one hundred and forty-four billion dollars.

lines.text: And that is exactly why Anthropic is going public. To keep paying for the future, it needs the deepest pool of capital on Earth.
lines.say: And that is exactly why Anthropic is going public. To keep paying for the future, it needs the deepest pool of capital on Earth.

lines.text: So let’s look at those three numbers one more time.
$16.3 billion in revenue: real demand.
lines.say: Sixteen point three billion in revenue. Real demand.

lines.text: $80.7 billion in losses: mostly a side effect of success.
lines.say: Eighty point seven billion in losses. Mostly, a side effect of success.

lines.text: $20.28 billion in cash: a snapshot, not a runway.
lines.say: Twenty point two eight billion in cash. A snapshot... not a runway.

lines.text: Anthropic’s strength is real. So is the bill.
lines.say: Anthropic's strength is real. So is the bill.

lines.text: The only question is which one grows faster.
